method: CHARLS has no PSU/strata, so analysis_plan §6 downgrade path: survey weights with model-based variance (NOT svyglm). Declared, not hidden.
findings: charls2011 current_smoking was mis-operationalised as the smoking rate AMONG EVER-SMOKERS (77.0%) because da061 is asked only of da059==1 — the third occurrence of the NHANES C1 error class. Corrected to 28.1%, which matches the Chinese reference.

The HbA1c reference for a Chinese population is ~5-7%, not the 11-13% OGTT/FPG figure: HbA1c-defined diabetes is roughly half of OGTT-defined diabetes in Chinese samples. Using the wrong prior would have flagged a correct variable as broken.

charls2015 smoking exposures fail the gate (current 7.5%, ever 12.4% vs references 27% and 40%) and are excluded. Resolving them requires the 2015 questionnaire codebook; until then no CHARLS smoking claim is supportable.

charls2015 hba1c_elevated is 13.1% vs 4.9% in 2011 — a 2.7-fold jump for the same variable name across waves, the same cross-wave comparability problem found for KNHANES HbA1c. The plan's 'borderline' CHARLS-2015 HbA1c x cataract signal therefore rests on a variable that is not comparable across waves.
This is the first time the CHARLS exposures were put through the codebook/prevalence gate.
